chunks: Yunus from Ibn Muskān from Sulaymān ibn Khālid said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would administer eighty (strikes) for intoxicating nabīdh, just as he would administer for wine, and he would execute in the third instance, just as he would execute the owner of wine.

key_terms.الثَّالِثَةِ: Al-thālithah: The third (instance/time, implying repeated consumption leading to execution).
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: Nabīdh: A traditional fermented drink, often from grapes or dates, which can become intoxicating.
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: Al-kamar: Wine/grape wine, the primary reference for intoxicants in Islamic law.
key_terms.الْمُسْكِرِ: Al-muskir: Intoxicating; that which causes intoxication.
key_terms.يَضْرِبُ: Yaḍribu: He strikes/administers (lashes as a legal punishment).

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for drinking intoxicating nabidh according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) establishes the equivalence between nabīdh and khamr in legal rulings, prescribing eighty lashes for the initial offense and execution for the third, reflecting the principle of 'kaffarah' (expiation) for intoxication. This ruling, recorded in al-Ishtibār, underscores the Shia scholarly view that the specific type of fermentation is secondary to the presence of intoxication (khamr) in determining the ḥadd punishment. It highlights the practical application of Quranic verses on intoxicants by extending the severe penalty to all fermented beverages that cause inebriation.
